title: Galaxy Tab S12 Leak Reveals Plus & Ultra Specs: Bigger Screens, Faster Chips, New Cameras
body:
Samsung’s next‑generation tablet line is beginning to take shape after a detailed leak surfaced, outlining the hardware specifications of the upcoming Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra. According to the information, the two devices will push the brand’s premium tablet performance further, offering up to 12 GB of RAM in the Plus model and a massive 16 GB in the Ultra, alongside high‑resolution AMOLED displays, upgraded processors, and expanded storage options. The revelations hint at a clear strategy to cement Samsung’s dominance in the high‑end Android tablet market ahead of the expected launch later this year.

The leaked data points to the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus featuring a 12.4‑inch Super AMOLED panel with a 2800 × 1752 pixel resolution and a 120 Hz refresh rate, mirroring the display quality of Samsung’s flagship smartphones. The device is said to be powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 for Galaxy, a chip that has already proven its mettle in the company’s latest smartphones, delivering a blend of performance and power efficiency suitable for multitasking, gaming, and content creation. Memory configurations will range from 8 GB to 12 GB of RAM, paired with 128 GB to 512 GB of UFS 3.1 storage, while a 10,090 mAh battery promises all‑day endurance with fast‑charging support.

The Ultra variant steps up the game with a larger 14.6‑inch Dynamic AMOLED display, sporting a 2960 × 1848 resolution and the same 120 Hz refresh rate, which should provide an immersive canvas for media consumption and professional workflows. The Ultra is expected to house the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 for Galaxy as well, but with a higher tier of 16 GB RAM and storage options extending up to 1 TB, positioning it as a direct competitor to Apple’s iPad Pro line. Battery capacity is rumored to be around 12,000 mAh, and the device will likely retain Samsung’s S Pen support with an upgraded latency of 2.5 ms, narrowing the gap with Apple’s Apple Pencil experience.

Analysts see these specifications as a response to a growing demand for high‑performance Android tablets that can double as laptop replacements. The inclusion of up to 16 GB of RAM and a 1 TB storage ceiling signals Samsung’s intention to attract power users—designers, video editors, and developers—who previously gravitated toward the iPad Pro for its raw capability. Moreover, the continuation of the S Pen’s low‑latency input and the potential for DeX desktop mode integration could make the Tab S12 series a compelling option for on‑the‑go productivity, especially in markets where Windows‑based tablets have struggled to gain traction.

The pricing strategy, while not disclosed, will be pivotal. Samsung’s previous premium tablets have sat in the $800‑$1,300 range, and the addition of top‑tier specs could push the Ultra beyond the $1,500 mark. If the company can balance cost with the promised performance, it may sway enterprise buyers and educational institutions that are increasingly looking for versatile, cross‑platform devices. Competition from Lenovo’s Tab P12 Pro and Huawei’s MatePad Pro series will also influence market dynamics, but Samsung’s brand equity and ecosystem—spanning smartphones, wearables, and smart home products—provide a strong platform for cross‑selling.

Looking ahead, the leak suggests that Samsung is set to unveil the Tab S12 lineup at a dedicated event later in 2024, likely aligning with its broader product roadmap that includes the Galaxy Z Fold 5 and the next generation of Galaxy Watch devices. Should the specifications hold true, the Tab S12 Plus and Ultra could redefine the Android tablet experience, offering a blend of high‑end display technology, robust processing power, and stylus precision that narrows the gap with Apple’s premium offerings. The industry will be watching closely as Samsung prepares to roll out what could become the benchmark for Android tablets in the years to come.
